prompt: Streaming platforms have largely replaced scheduled television and, for many people, trips to the cinema. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this change.
essay:
The convenience argument is settled and not very interesting. Of course it is better to watch a programme when you are free than when a scheduler decides you are; nobody who has waited a week for an episode wants that week back. The change worth examining is what happens to the things being watched, and to the fact that we are no longer watching them together.

On the production side, the shift has been genuinely liberating in one direction and quietly constricting in another. A series in Korean or Danish can now find a global audience without a broadcaster in each country deciding in advance that its viewers would not tolerate subtitles, and work that would once have been deleted from an archive stays available indefinitely. Against that, platforms commission from behavioural data, and data is necessarily a record of what has already happened. The result is a catalogue that is wide but strangely uniform: enormous choice among things that resemble other things.

The loss that receives least attention is simultaneity. A programme broadcast to a whole country at once produced something no library of on-demand titles can — a conversation the next morning that nobody had to arrange, between participants who had not chosen each other. That was never the point of broadcasting, but it was one of its effects, and it is gone. Cinema attendance matters for a related reason: a film watched among strangers in the dark is a different experience from the same film watched with a phone within reach, and the second is not simply a portable version of the first.

So the advantages are real and belong to viewers, while the disadvantages are structural and belong to everyone, including the viewers who cannot see them. I would not restore the schedule. But it is worth saying that we have traded a shared, imposed, occasionally boring culture for a private and infinitely responsive one, and that the second is better in almost every respect except the ones that only become visible once they are missing.
title: Streaming instead of schedules and cinemas
